THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the XX Additional Small Causes Judge & XVIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate & Member,
MACT, Bengaluru (henceforth referred to as 'tribunal' for short) in MVC No.4011/2018 dated 21.10.2019.
2.

XX Additional Small Causes Judge & XVIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate & Member,
MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimant was standing near Kannika Parameshwari temple, Kuvempu road, Kengeri, on 08.07.2018 at 08:30 p.m., during which time, the driver of the Ecosport car bearing registration No.KA-41-MA-0762 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came in a high speed and dashed against the claimant.
Due to the impact, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He incurred financial expenditures at a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- for his medical NC:
2024:KHC:7762 treatment and other miscellaneous expenses.
It is stated that he was hale and healthy prior to the accident and was working as a coolie and earning a sum of Rs.700/- per day.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident and disability suffered, he has lost his future earning capacity.
Hence, he filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

3. Respondent No.1 was placed exparte and respondent No.2/insurance company filed statement of objections, denying the claim made by the claimant, including age, avocation, income and the negligence attributed as against the offending car and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. To substantiate the claim of the claimant, he was examined himself as PW.1 and he examined a doctor as PW.2 and produced documents as Exs.P1 to P13.
The respondent No.2 neither adduced evidence nor produced documents.

sentences.text: On the basis of oral and documentary evidence placed on record, the tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.3,80,599/- along with interest at 6% per annum to be paid by the respondent No.2/insurance company within 90 days.
NC: 2024:KHC:7762 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company.
Perused the impugned judgment and award.
7. Exs.
P1 to P7
are the police records.
Exs. P8
to P13 are the medical records for having incurred financial expenditures for the treatment of claimant.
On perusal of the police records, it is seen that an FIR and a charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the offending car.
Having considered the material on record, the negligence is rightly attributed as against the driver of the offending car.
8. Now coming to the question of age, avocation, income and the disability of the claimant, the age of the claimant as on date of occurrence of the accident was 32 years.
The multiplier applicable would be '16' which is rightly applied by the tribunal and same does not call for interference.
The doctor has been examined as PW.2.
He has opined that the claimant has suffered disability to an extent of 12% to the NC: 2024:KHC:7762 whole body which is 1/3rd of the disability to the particular limb.

Whereas, disability to the whole body has not been expressed by the tribunal,
therefore, on the basis of the government gazette notification, has deducted 1/3rd and has taken disability at 12% which does not call for interference.
9. The tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month, as no documentary evidence was produced.

However, the notional income prescribed by the legal services authority chart for the year 2018 is at a sum of Rs.12,500/- and the same is taken as income for the purpose of computation of loss of future earning capacity.

10. In view of the above, loss of future earning due to disability would be a sum of Rs.2,88,000/-
(Rs.12,500 x 12 x 16 x 12%) as against a sum of Rs.2,30,400/- awarded by the tribunal.

11. A sum of Rs.25,000/- was awarded by the tribunal towards pain and suffering, the claimant as suffered fracture of left lower limb, hence an additional sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under this head.
Towards medical expenses a sum of NC: 2024:KHC:7762 Rs.70,199/- was awarded, on the basis of actual medical bills produced at Exs.P9 and P10 and the same is retained.

Towards food,
conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded by the tribunal and the same is retained.

Towards loss of amenities, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
and the same is on the lower side, hence, an additional sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

Towards future medical expenses, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded, whereas the doctor - PW2 has opined that the requirement of a sum of Rs.40,000/- to 45,000/- for removal of implant, hence,
an additional sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under this head.
The tribunal has not awarded any amount towards loss of income during laid up period.

In view of this Court enhancing the income at a sum of Rs.12,500/- per month and a period of three months would be required for recovering from Gurunatha @ Gururaj Badiger vs Kuldeep Sharma on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55775367/
3 the injuries sustained by the claimant and get back to normal day to day activities.

sentences.text: Hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.37,500/- under this head.

12. In view of the discussions made hereinabove, the claimant would be entitled to compensation of Rs.5,15,699/- as against Rs.3,80,599/-
NC: 2024:KHC:7762 13.

Accordingly I pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award passed by the tribunal in MVC No.4011/2018 dated 21.10.2019 is modified and the claimant is entitled for a compensation of Rs.5,15,699/- along with interest at 6% per annum.
(iii) The enhanced compensation shall be paid within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
(iv) Entire compensation amount shall be disbursed and released in favour of the claimant upon proper identification.
